Glaze recipes, step by step: "sand satin"

Version 2026-11-07 · the 🧪 Glaze recipes page (card G) with the Auto engine, driven in a browser through every kind of input, from a colour alone to words + photo + formula. Every screenshot is the real page; every number is the page's own result (a test copy of the app with its own logs).

red frame = where to look (the inside stays see-through) · orange = from test_similarity.zip (the team's colour-match model and its rules) · purple = from the text branch · black = the Glaze Search project

The three engines, and how Auto picks one

Auto useswhen you givescore of a recipemodels and data
Colour rankingonly a colour0 × learned + 0.80 × colour + 0.10 × surface + 0.10 × cone the colour score exp(−ΔE00/20), surface and cone rules and the 6,718-recipe catalog; the learned part is switched off (no model)
Colour matchcolour + cone / surface menus, no words0.40 × learned + 0.40 × colour + 0.10 × surface + 0.10 cone all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (frozen) reads the template color: …, Cone …, …, unknown, unknown → text head 384→256; recipes: 26 oxides → √ → PCA-16 → chemistry head 16→256; learned = (cos + 1)/2 in their 256-d latent space
Smart searchtyped words, a photo object or a formulaits own weights (words 0.35 · photo 0.35 · formula 0.25 · colour 0.30 · cone 0.10 · surface 0.10 · transparency 0.05 · atmosphere 0.05), divided by the total of the parts you gave MiniLM + DINOv2 (frozen) + oxides → trained heads in one 256-d space, trained with the team's method (masked InfoNCE, composition groups); recipe text = colour word + tags cleaned by the text branch
colour value = exp(−ΔE00 / 20)  ·  learned / words / photo / formula value = (cosine + 1) / 2  ·  surface, cone = 1 when they match, 0 when not or unknown  ·  score = Σ weight × value (0 – 1)

Case 1 · Only a colour → colour ranking

  1. Leave the words empty; type the HEX #C2B280 (sand) in 2 · Choose a colour.
  2. Leave cone and surface on "any"; 4 · How to search stays on Auto. Press Find recipes.

Case 2 · Colour + the menus, no words → Colour match (the team's model, 4 / 4 / 1 / 1)

  1. 2a: keep the sand colour and choose surface Satin in 3 · Firing and surface. Find recipes.
  2. 2b: also choose cone 6. Find recipes.

#1 has no surface and no cone on record, so both count 0; it still wins on colour (ΔE00 1.4) and the learned match. That is why 2a mixes in cone-9 and unknown-surface recipes.

Case 3b · + a photo → Smart search with the photo

  1. 📷 My photo: upload the Manual's test-tile photo (Glazy #614435). The app finds the tiles and takes the main colour of the selected one.
  2. Press 🧪 Find glaze recipes for this colour: the recipes page searches with the photo object, its colour and the words already typed.

Read with care: this photo is in the database, so finding its own recipe (Satin matte base glaze, #614435) at #1 is expected, not proof. Its surface on Glazy is Satin-matte, not Satin, so the surface part is 0. The app took the large warm-grey tile (#8B7770); for the sand glaze, click the yellow tile and use 🎨 Pick colour.

Case 3c · Only a formula → Smart search on the formula

  1. Untick text, colour and photo object in 4 · How to search.
  2. Open the formula card, paste SiO₂ 44.0 · Al₂O₃ 16.8 · CaO 9.7 · MgO 7.0 · Na₂O 2.9 · B₂O₃ 2.8 · K₂O 0.8 (the real formula of #614435, with subscripts) and press Fill: 'formula' is ticked automatically. Find recipes.

The calculation of #1

partweightvalueweight × valuewhat the value is
formula1.0000.8780.878(cos + 1) / 2 of your formula and the recipe in the joint space
score of #1 Magnesium Matte base0.878
  • Magnesium Matte base · 0.878 · oatmeal #BEB8AA · cone 6 · Semi-matte
  • Marci's Matte (Selsor White Matte) · 0.874 · off white #E9E2D6 · cone 6 · Matte
  • Evan's Magnesium Matte Color Run · 0.860 · oatmeal #C4BCB0 · cone 5 - 7 · Matte

What it shows: the formula alone finds the high-magnesium matte family (MgO 7 %): every result is matte without any colour or surface given, because the chemistry predicts the surface. The recipe itself is not #1: the formula is compared with each recipe's combined text, photo and formula fingerprint.

  • Only a colour: exact colour, nothing else controlled. With the menus: always set the cone.
  • Typed words give the best list without a photo; with a photo, leave colour words out of the text (they replace the photo's colour).
  • A formula needs at least 3 oxides including a flux; subscripts (SiO₂) are read. Alone, it finds the chemistry family.
  • A database photo finds its own recipe: that is expected, not a test of the model.
